articles.title_original: Suspect arrested after historic town hall set alight - French media
articles.title_zh: Suspect arrested after historic town hall set alight - French media
facts_zh:
Suspect arrested after historic town hall set alight - French media
- Published
A suspect linked to a far-left movement has been arrested in France after a 19th Century city hall was gutted by a fire over the weekend that broke out during mass disorder, French media report.
The clock tower and parts of the roof of the ornate city hall in the central city of Limoges were engulfed in flames before collapsing on Saturday.
The 34-year-old suspect is known to police for acts of violence against public officials and is on a French national security watchlist, FranceInfo and BFM TV report.

all_titles.en: Suspect arrested after historic town hall set alight - French media

articles.title_original: Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says
articles.title_zh: Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says
facts_zh:
Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says
- Published
The eldest son of Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie, convicted of murdering 191 people, says his younger siblings were still being forced to fast as recently as two weeks ago.
Dan Mackenzie, 27, said he reported the case to police, who rescued eight children, including his five younger siblings from their grandmother's house, and took them to a rescue centre.
"They were basically forcibly fasted because they were denying food to them for almost three days," he tells BBC's Newsday.

all_titles.en: Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says

articles.title_zh: Marseille braces for more unrest after protests give way to 'apocalyptic' disorder
facts_zh:
Marseille braces for more unrest after protests give way to 'apocalyptic' disorder
- Published
Thunder and lightning have boomed across Marseille following the weekend's mayhem, illuminating the cracked windows and boarded-up doors of hundreds of businesses that were smashed as protests gave way to disorder.
France's second city saw some of the worst violence as chaos gripped the country on Saturday.
Local business leaders say more than 500 premises were damaged, and the majority looted.

articles.title_zh: Man charged with attack on Australian MP as suspect's father says she is family friend
facts_zh:
Man charged with attack on Australian MP as suspect's father says she is family friend
- Published
A 43-year-old man has been charged after Australian MP Helen Haines was hit by a car in the state of Victoria on Monday.

The suspect will appear in court on Wednesday to face charges of dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official.
Local media earlier named the alleged attacker as environmental activist Brendan Nugent.

Curfew imposed in parts of central Paris and other cities after rioting across France
- Published
French authorities have imposed overnight curfews in parts of central Paris and other cities after a weekend of riots and looting across the country.

Police in Paris said a curfew would be in force between 23:00 local time (21:00 GMT) and 06:00 in Place de la République, where protesters had gathered over the weekend, and the Les Halles shopping area.
A ban on unauthorised gatherings has also been imposed in several other parts of the city centre.
